articles.title: Google Is Killing Google Assistant on Android Devices Next Month
articles.summary: Google announced the plan to sunset Assistant last year, but things were pushed back as users found Gemini not entirely capable of filling Assistant's shoes. During this time, if Gemini wasn't able to handle a particular request, it would default back to Assistant to get the job done. Users could also opt-out of Gemini and stick to the older program if they wanted.  After September 4, that won't be an option anymore.
articles.body:
Google is killing off Google Assistant on Android devices starting on September 4, replacing the service with Gemini. This means that voice-controlled assistant tasks – the sort of thing summoned up with a "Hey Google" – will now be routed through Gemini instead of the older service.

Gemini is undoubtedly more powerful than the older Assistant, able to hold a conversation, make suggestions, and answer complex questions in the same way as other LLM-powered AI chatbots. But it can also be less reliable, sometimes making incorrect assumptions, going off on a tangent, or forgetting it has the capability to do the task you've asked of it. It's also often slower, taking time to "think" about the request, regardless of how complex it is.

Assistant, on the other hand, was less powerful but more reliable. I use Assistant myself, but mostly for simple tasks like setting a kitchen timer, controlling lights, and shutting off alarms. Not exactly the kind of things that need the power of an LLM to get done.

A Reddit thread discussing the news is filled with users lamenting the change.

"Wanted to call my father while I was driving, so I told Gemini to call him. It gave me the definition of the word "father" instead of calling him," said one user . "Went back to Google Assistant immediately. Please Google, don't force me to switch to Gemini... I hate it."

"Gemini makes me unlock the phone to change the temperature. It's useless," said another .

Google announced the plan to sunset Assistant last year, but things were pushed back as users found Gemini not entirely capable of filling Assistant's shoes. During this time, if Gemini wasn't able to handle a particular request, it would default back to Assistant to get the job done. Users could also opt-out of Gemini and stick to the older program if they wanted.

After September 4, that won't be an option anymore.

The change currently only applies to Android devices and the accessories that connect to them, like Wear OS watches, headphones, and cars with Android Auto. Google Home speakers and smart devices, as well as Google TVs and cars with Google will retain access to Google Assistant for now, though Gemini is already available on most of those devices as well, and I wouldn't be surprised if Assistant support is ultimately discontinued there too.

Assistant now joins the long list of products and services that Google has killed off over the years. Meanwhile, AI continues to make gaming worse , driving up hardware prices and leading us to a world where consoles are prohibitively expensive . But hey, at least Google can juice those Gemini user numbers a bit more.

Bo Moore is IGN's Senior Manager of Tech. You can find him online @usebomswisely.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Official IKEA Mod Features Matt Berry as a Kallax Storage Companion
articles.summary: What We Do in the Shadows' Matt Berry voices an IKEA Kallax bookcase in a free official Creation for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.
articles.body:
What We Do in the Shadows' Matt Berry voices an IKEA Kallax bookcase in a free official Creation for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim .

The infamous IKEA storage unit will become a fully-fledged in-game companion, Kallax Storageborn, able to carry your items and prevent you becoming easily over-encumbered. You'll even be able to summon him with a custom Dragon Shout (AYE-KEY-YAH). Yes, IKEA.

Why is Berry being roped in to lend his baritone boom to a bookcase? Well, this is an officially-licensed IKEA collaboration that plays on the infamous annoyance of being over-encumbered within the game.

All Male Marriage Partners in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

But there's seemingly more here than just a simple joke. Not only have Berry's talents been secured, but developer Kinggath Creations has crafted a full quest with two new IKEA-themed dungeons, and a boss fight against the Clutter Golem. Need help assembling your inventory? You'll also be able to wield the Dwemer Allen Key weapon, wear the Meatball Helmet, and gobble meatball food items.

"At IKEA, we believe in creating a better everyday life for the many people — and why shouldn't that include their digital lives?" said IKEA exec Kemi Anthony. "Skyrim possesses one of the largest modding communities in gaming, and we saw a space where our expertise in functional storage could make a real difference in this fantasy world.

"Matt Berry's distinctive, legendary voice brings theatrics, booming authority and charm to the new Creation. In bringing Kallax to life we hope to not only make a meaningful difference for Skyrim players but doing so with a touch of added IKEA playfulness to delight gamers who've long been bogged down by too much stuff."

This isn't Berry's first video game credit, of course. You can hear his dulcet tones right now in LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight as Bane, or in the celebrated 2024 British indie adventure Thank Goodness You're Here!

It's a busy time for Berry, who is due to appear next year in both Sonic the Hedgehog 4 and A Minecraft Movie Squared. This year, he'll appear as The Fish in a new Bill Hader-starring adaptation of The Cat in the Hat.

The IKEA Kallax Storageborn add-on Creation will be available to download for free via Bethesda Game Studios in-game Creations menu from today, September 9.

Your desert oasis (hence the name) will face "natural disasters, cyber warfare, and fragile political alliances between neighboring settlements," according to the small indie team behind the project.

The inter-corporate shenanigans extend beyond that, too, as you'll "launch cyberattacks against rival infrastructure, manage loyalty levels, negotiate loans, detect spies, and manipulate economic conditions."

articles.title: Monster Hunter Wilds Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date Set for December 2026
articles.summary: Capcom has announced a Monster Hunter Wilds Nintendo Switch 2 release date of December 4, 2026.
articles.body:
Capcom has announced a Monster Hunter Wilds Nintendo Switch 2 release date of December 4, 2026.

The latest entry in the publisher’s monster-hunting series kicked off today’s September 2026 Nintendo Direct. Additional details about the release include confirmation that the Switch 2 version of Monster Hunter Wilds will come with local play and all previous title updates.

Capcom announced earlier this year that Monster Hunter Wilds was Switch 2 bound but declined to share a specific release date. It led some to believe we may have to wait until next year to get our hands on the game, making today's December announcement a nice surprise.

"Venture into the Forbidden Lands to track and hunt massive monsters, craft gear, and uncover the mysteries of an ever-changing world," Nintendo said. "Whether playing at home or on the go, hunters can team up locally via wireless play or join friends online with full cross-platform multiplayer support. All Title Update content is included, such as the Grand Hub, fan-favorite monsters like Mizutsune and Lagiacrus, the FINAL FANTASY XIV Online collaboration, and more. Monster Hunter Wilds launches for Nintendo Switch 2 on Dec. 4."

Nintendo has also confirmed that Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance will come to Switch 2 at some point in 2027. The expansion is expected to come to PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S at some point next year, too, though it's unclear if it will receive a simultaneous launch across all platforms.

A Switch 2 port for Monster Hunter Wilds is something fans have been looking forward to for a while. Capcom launched its latest installment all the way back in February 2025, meaning Nintendo fans will be fast approaching the game's second anniversary by the time it actually launches for the hybrid sequel console. It's hard to say if the wait will have been worth it, but those who have spent the last few months hoping to see it arrive sooner rather than later will surely be happy to see it out so soon.

Monster Hunter Wilds Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date Trailer - Screenshots

IGN gave Monster Hunter Wilds an 8/10 review . At the time we said it "continues to smooth off the rougher corners of the series in smart ways, making for some extremely fun fights but also lacking any real challenge."

articles.title: Nintendo Confirms Pikmin 4 Switch 2 Edition
articles.summary: Nintendo has announced Pikmin 4: Switch 2 Edition, an enhanced version of the brilliant real-time strategy game with new content and upgraded visuals.
articles.body:
Nintendo has announced Pikmin 4: Switch 2 Edition, an enhanced version of the brilliant real-time strategy game with new content and upgraded visuals launching on November 12.

You can use voice commands to chat and move Oatchi. A new mode, Dandori Academy, will see you racing against the clock to complete treasure hunts before time runs out. This offering is all about high scores, with three difficulty options and weekly challenges every Friday, Saturday and Sunday. 72 Dandori Academy stages will be available over time.

The brilliant Pikmin 4 originally launched for the original Switch back in July 2023, and was greeted by a warm response from fans and critics alike. Still, the game never received any additional post-launch content, even though it sold well in comparison to its predecessors (particularly in Japan, where Pikmin 4 beat the launch sales of the series' previous three installments combined).

Once again, Pikmin 4 follows a team of explorers setting foot on an alien world (that's actually Earth), aided by a horde of helpful creatures (that's your Pikmin). This fourth major game adds indoor and night-time gameplay, as well as a useful dog-like companion (named Oatchi) who smoothes over some of the series' fussier gameplay.

In short, Pikmin 4 revives and enhances the series' best features to provide the best and most complete-feeling Pikmin game to date, with the return of Pikmin 2's dungeon-like caves and the inclusion of every major Pikmin species all very welcome. It's also a very generous game already in terms of content, with unlockable side-modes and a fun story campaign, that will now become more generous still.

articles.title: Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity Is Coming to Switch 2 With a Discount for Existing Owners
articles.summary: Nintendo has announced a Nintendo Switch 2 edition of Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity.
articles.body:
Nintendo has announced a Nintendo Switch 2 edition of Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity.

The remaster was announced during the new Nintendo Direct and will release on February 25. The definitive edition will feature enhanced visuals, 60FPS, more enemies on-screen, all DLC from the original version, a harder difficulty mode, and a discount for existing owners on Switch 1. You'll also be able to transfer your save data, making it all the more convenient. The exact discount has yet to be revealed, but more details will be shared soon.

For those who have never played it, Age of Calamity serves as sort of a prequel to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. It ultimately diverges into a different timeline and therefore its place in the canon is debated among fans, but many of its events still inform a lot of elements in Breath of the Wild. As a result, it's not required playing in order to understand Breath of the Wild, but it may enhance the experience a bit.

Age of Calamity also has a different style of gameplay from traditional Zelda games, as it's much more of a hack and slash game. The Switch 1 version was largely well-liked, but was heavily criticized for performance issues. It seems like the Switch 2 version will directly address this critique with the inclusion of 60FPS, while also enhancing the amount of action on screen.

It has been a big week for Zelda fans, as we also got a glimpse at the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The remake is set to release on November 5 and will likely be one of the biggest releases of the fall.

Viral hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon is sneaking onto Nintendo Switch 2 – and it’s out today.

The indie developer behind the popular PC video game, lemorion_1224, confirmed the news during today’s September 2026 Nintendo Direct. Instead of waiting to check out Meccha Chameleon with a later release date, it was confirmed that players will be able to paint themselves into the experience starting today.

articles.title: I spent an hour riding inside Tesla’s steering-wheel-free Cybercab
articles.summary: We tested out the Tesla Cybercab, and discovered some issues with the butterfly doors and bizarre drop-off locations. Otherwise, it was an impressive experience.
articles.body: Getting out of a taxi shouldn’t be a shameful experience. Yet I find myself feeling particularly embarrassed while exiting a Tesla Cybercab as it partially blocks a narrow road outside a popular Austin swimming hole. As a cadre of annoyed, sweaty Texan parking spot hunters pile up around it, the gold-painted two-seater just sits there obliviously, lights flashing. I try not to make eye contact, but I can feel the stares of frustrated pool-goers around me, whose earnest attempt at a peaceful outdoor reprieve from the heat had just been interrupted by yet another not-quite-finished glimpse into the future. Tesla’s long-awaited, two-seater Cybercab is officially offering paid rides in Austin, Texas, and the experience, so far, somehow feels equal parts nerve-wracking and reassuringly boring — often at the same time. The Verge spent the better part of an hour in the gilded hype-mobile last weekend, gallivanting around a roughly 288-square-mile geofenced area of the Texas capital. At its best, the service offers one of the clearest glimpses yet of a near future where autonomous vehicles feel less like a retrofitted version of the cars we know now and more like purpose-built autonomous lounges, free of steering wheels or pedals. But long wait times, reported issues with the butterfly doors, and traffic-jam-inducing drop-off locations muddy the picture. And while nothing went seriously wrong during my rides, the self-driving software also didn’t feel as confident as you would like in a car with no manual controls. It felt more like a slightly stoned teenager, nervously braking, indecisively bobbing between lanes, and seemingly second-guessing some of its decisions. There’s also an unavoidable Elon Musk–shaped cloud hanging over every ride, attracting angry eyeballs and carrying all the political baggage that comes with anything he touches. [Image: [Image: [Image: Want a Cybercab? Get ready to wait Cybercabs aren’t hard to miss, with their ostentatious gold color, Blade Runner–esque aesthetic, and dinner plate–like wheel coverings. I first saw them testing around Austin earlier this year with a human safety driver and retrofitted with steering wheel and pedals. As of today, the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles says 45 Cybercabs are registered in the state. Tesla has a lot riding on its newest vehicle. For years, Musk has hyped the imminent arrival of fully autonomous vehicles, arguing that “going balls to the wall for autonomy” was an obvious move for Tesla. The company launched its Robotaxi service last year with a fleet of self-driving Model Ys, to mixed results. But Cybercab presents a potentially much bigger bet. An entire fleet of purpose-built vehicles designed specifically to offer unsupervised driving as a service. I requested my first Cybercab ride from Tesla’s Robotaxi app around 6PM on Friday evening. It’s a good thing I didn’t have anywhere to be. The app listed an hour-plus wait time for a $15 ride under two miles, though the actual wait was about 45 minutes. (The next two wait times were about 40 and 25 minutes, respectively). The car pulled up across the street from my house, flashing under its front bumper to signal it was picking up a passenger. [Video: cybercab] As someone with a less-than-stellar history with Model Y doors, I was glad the Cybercab instead let users open the butterfly-style doors by tapping a button on the mobile app. A handful of passengers have reported those same doors opening up so quickly that they end up striking them, though I never experienced that issue. The interior, a single row of two chairs separated by a cup holder, feels spacious for public transit but cramped for a private car. That’s helped somewhat by the extra legroom where a steering wheel and pedals would be. It has a sparse, minimalist gray fabric interior, save for a massive center touchscreen. That screen serves as a command center, showing a real time-3D rendering of the trip, including surrounding cars and pedestrians. It’s also how you start the ride. Once rolling, the screen doubles as an entertainment hub. I linked my Spotify, Netflix, and YouTube accounts, and tested the built-in Arcade app with an external PlayStation controller. Yes, you can game your way through a busy intersection if you really want to be that guy. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The first ride took about 15 minutes. Almost immediately, the windshield wipers switched on, despite it being a sunny, 95-degree day. That wasn’t the only oddity. About halfway through the trip, the Cybercab crossed an underpass leading into downtown, a route I take almost every day. Instead of staying in the lane to go straight, it switched into one that would’ve forced a left turn onto the highway. It corrected itself, but not before a handful of cars passed by. Again, the wipers wiped. When it’s not second-guessing itself, the Cybercab’s moment-to-moment ride feels welcomely smooth. The vehicle itself is both zippy and comfortable. For a quick comparison, I requested a Waymo home and felt that, purely from a comfort standpoint, the Cybercab had a noticeable leg up. Legroom, ride quality, the app’s simplicity and usability, and in-cabin entertainment options all felt like a move in the right direction. In terms of price, fares were around the same as a typical base Uber, between $15–$21 over three trips. Riding in the Cybercab draws a great deal of attention, some endearing, some less so. Pedestrians downtown (especially kids) stopped and pointed, sometimes doing a double take at the sight of me in the driver’s seat with no wheel in front of me. One driver in the lane next to me, eyes wide, signaled for me to lower my window. When I did, he gestured with his arms and asked, “No steering wheel?” I said no pedals either, to which he responded with an emphatic, “Damn, bro!” There also aren’t any mirrors, which makes the already confined, teardrop-shaped shell feel all the more closed off, especially when sitting on the driver’s side. As someone used to unconsciously checking mirrors while driving, having them removed feels like having your peripheral vision suddenly cut off. It’s unnerving, especially with cars passing by. What’s more concerning is the Cybercab’s at times bizarre choice of drop-off spots. Several riders posted videos over the weekend of the cab stopping in the middle of busy roads, in some cases without even pulling to the curb. As mentioned above, I experienced a brief example of that after being dropped off at Austin’s popular Barton Springs. These aren’t the massive lane-closing errors that have occurred with other AVs, but they are awkward and common enough to stand out. They also won’t help win over other drivers, a majority of whom still feel uncomfortable around driverless cars. Another Tesla, another regulatory controversy In true Tesla fashion, the Cybercab is already courting controversy. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an Audit Query almost immediately after paid rides began, examining how Tesla self-certified that the car without a steering wheel or pedals complies with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. Competitors like Zoox, whose vehicles also lack those conventional controls, faced a similar audit years ago before ultimately pursuing and receiving a formal exemption. Tesla pressed forward with its Cybercab rollout without seeking that exemption. NHTSA said it doesn’t comment on active investigations when asked for comment by The Verge. Tesla did not respond to a request for comment. The next few weeks and months in Austin could determine how fast Tesla can expand its Cybercab vision. Musk says he intends to grow operations nationwide, and vehicles have already been spotted in Orlando and parked outside Miami International Airport. But any Cybercab crash or other high-profile mistake made in its politically friendly home state risks drawing even more regulatory scrutiny and setting back expansion timelines. And with competitors like Zoox also rolling out purpose-built AVs, delays are something Tesla really can’t afford. Images by Mack DeGuerin / The Verge

articles.title: Mario Kart World Update to Add Classic Tracks for Free Later Today
articles.summary: Nintendo has revealed that a Mario Kart World update will add classic SNES tracks, Knockout Tour courses, and more later today.
articles.body:
Nintendo has revealed that a Mario Kart World update will add classic SNES tracks, Knockout Tour courses, and more today.

The company announced the news as part of its September 2026 Nintendo Direct today. While there are no new playable characters or outfits in Mario Kart World (yet), the new update should arrive as a welcome surprise to players who have been looking for a reason to grab the wheel following its Nintendo Switch 2 launch last summer.

A total of 10 classic courses have been added as part of the update. As a bonus, these courses feature old-school item tiles instead of the flashier floating boxes. For the Knockout Tour courses, players can look forward to two new routes to race through.

A free update for Mario Kart World launches later today! Play 10 classic courses from Super Mario Kart in VS Race mode and two new Knockout tour routes. #NintendoDirect Get the update: pic.twitter.com/1FIL2jzzQY — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) September 9, 2026

A free update for Mario Kart World launches later today! Play 10 classic courses from Super Mario Kart in VS Race mode and two new Knockout tour routes. #NintendoDirect Get the update: pic.twitter.com/1FIL2jzzQY

"Classic courses from Super Mario Kart have been hiding in plain sight across the continent of Mario Kart World, and now 10 of them can be played as standalone races in VS Race," Nintendo said in a press release. "Tear through Choco Island, Vanilla Lake, Ghost Valley and more, complete with ? Panels that grant items just like in the Super NES original. The update also adds two new Knockout Tour routes, Propeller Rally and Turnip Rally, plus a Spectator Mode when playing with friends online or via LAN Play."

Everything shown during today's Nintendo Direct trailer will arrive when Mario Kart World update 1.8.0 launches free for Switch 2 players later today. Patch notes for the update are already available, so you can see the full list of every classic track joining with the update below.

articles.title: The Switch 2 is getting a 2D Metroid called Ravenous
articles.summary: Nintendo just announced a new 2D entry in the Metroid series for the Switch 2 titled Metroid Ravenous. It launches on January 28th, 2027.
articles.body: Nintendo just announced a new 2D entry in the Metroid series for the Switch 2, titled Metroid Ravenous. It’s launching on January 28th, 2027. The new game looks like an evolution of Metroid Dread. While it’s still a 2D game, it features 3D graphics, lots of cinematic action shots, parrying enemies, and Samus rolling around in Morph Ball form. What’s new for this game is that Samus also appears to somehow absorb energy from enemies to survive — Nintendo’s marketing copy for the game uses the line “eat or be eaten.” There are also many fearsome-looking foes, including some giant creatures and a group of futuristic, caped fighters that attack Samus with blades and spinning metal hats. Ravenous is the latest game in what’s been something of a resurgence for the Metroid series. Nintendo launched Dread in 2021, a remaster of Metroid Prime for the original Switch in 2023, and Metroid Prime 4 last year.

articles.title: Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 Remakes Are Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 Very Soon
articles.summary: The remakes of Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 are coming to Nintendo Switch 2 next month.
articles.body:
The remakes of Resident Evil 2 , 3, and 4 are coming to Nintendo Switch 2 next month.

Capcom is making sure fans can enjoy classic Resident Evil games on the go by porting the trilogy of remakes over to Nintendo Switch 2. The games were announced for the console durign today's Nintendo Direct and will arrive digitally on October 16, with physical versions to follow on in January 2027.

These won't be sold exclusively as a collection (though it wouldn't be surprising if there is a bundle), so fans will be able to pick which ones they want to purchase and play.

Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 will come with their respective DLCs, including 4's Separate Ways expansion that follows Ada Wong. No other unique features or upgrades were mentioned, so don't expect any radical changes if you've already played these remakes elsewhere. Nevertheless, it's a great offering for those who either want to revisit them portably or play them for the first time.

The bulk of the mainline, numbered Resident Evil games will be natively available on the platform once these release, as Capcom previously released Resident Evil 7, Village, and Requiem for the console. Of course, we're still missing native versions of Resident Evil 1, 5, and 6, but all three of those games are available on Switch 1 and playable on Switch 2 through the console's backward compatibility. As a result, fans can play the entire Resident Evil saga on Switch 2, which is nothing to scoff at.

The next Resident Evil remake will be for Code Veronica . The game — now just Resident Evil Veronica — was announced at Summer Game Fest, though details are still relatively scarce on the project. It is currently scheduled to be released next year and, yes, it will also launch for Nintendo Switch 2.

Catch up on all of the big announcements in our roundup of everything announced in today's Nintendo Direct broadcast , as well as everything announced in The Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct that aired yesterday.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, and 10 Other Games We Loved at PAX Last Weekend
articles.summary: In this roundup of our favorite games from the show, we're spotlighting some of the most eye-grabbing titles we saw during PAX West 2026 and other adjacent events such as The Media Indie Exchange. Along with Final Fantasy 7 Revelation and Persona 4 Revival, we're also spotlighting some new games that just may be your next favorite game to play.
articles.body:
With the remainder of 2026 and early 2027 packed with new and exciting games, the latest PAX West offered attendees a great way to see some of the most anticipated new titles a bit early. Coming hot on the heels of Gamescom 2026 and only a few months before Grand Theft Auto 6's release, attendees got a final public look at a wide variety of big games, some of which are still flying under players' radar.

In this roundup of our favorite games from the show, we're spotlighting some of the most eye-grabbing titles we saw during PAX West 2026 and other adjacent events such as The Media Indie Exchange. Along with Final Fantasy VII Revelation and Persona 4 Revival, we're also spotlighting some new games that just may be your next favorite game to play.

We have played and seen much of Final Fantasy VII Revelation in recent weeks, and it's doing well to set the stage for what will likely be the Final Fantasy series' most ambitious entry to date. Focusing on the climax of Cloud and crew's globe-trotting journey to take down Sephiroth and save the world, FFVII Revelation not only brings the full party together -- finally giving Cid and Vincent their time to shine -- but it also modernizes the original game's open-world moment by giving players full control over which activities to take on and locations they'll travel to. With Gamescom and the recent State of Play giving us an impressive look at the expanded open world and deeper combat reworks, Revelation is shaping up to be a conclusion that will make the 11-year wait for the full Final Fantasy VII Remake worth it, bringing the ambitious and large-scale FFVII Remake saga to an explosive finish.

For more on Final Fantasy VII Revelation , check back with IGN for our upcoming full-length preview.

As the saying goes, what's old is new again. The recent influx of new games recreating the early era of 3D games from the PlayStation 1, Sega Saturn, and Nintendo 64 has shown there's so much more to appreciate about classic 3D games. That's where Dungeon Lurker 's moody, fourth-wall-breaking take on a PS1-style action-RPG is laying out its alluring concept. Taking on the role of an unknown player revisiting a recently passed friend's favorite game, you'll dive into Dungeon Lurker 's eerie dungeon-crawling adventure to power up the hero and earn new skills to brave the dangers below.

But as you dive deeper into the game and examine your friend's notes written into its manual from the seemingly safe boundaries of your living room, it'll become apparent that the game itself might be haunted, leaving you to uncover the source of the supernatural presence that's drawn you in. It's equal parts a legit dungeon-crawler beat-em-up, a throwback to classic 3D action games, and a dash of a supernatural horror game -- and Dungeon Crawler handles all parts with a compelling grace that had me hooked on what's to come next.

The Beyond the Western Deep comic series is a cult favorite within the indie comic space – and now, the creators of the comics and developer Sungrove Studios are building the fantasy series' first video game. War of the Western Deep leans into the style of classic 2D adventure games like King's Quest and The Secret of Monkey Island , where players guide Mirren as they traverse through enemy territory and fight against bandits and invading northerners to make it back to the kingdom of Sungrove.

What immediately pulled me in was the fantastic, expressive art style that feels like a mash-up of Disney's Robin Hood and classic Don Bluth animation, lending so much personality and charm to the world -- all while adding in Game of Thrones-style intrigue into the mix. War of the Western Deep was one of the most impressive 2D games at PAX West, and seeing its hand-crafted animation come to life in an adventure game has me eager to see what's to come with the full game.

Simply put, Persona 4 is one of the great modern JRPGs, and it's exciting to see it get a well-deserved remake. Much like Persona 3 Reload , Persona 4 Revival aims to give the original game's demon-slaying, high school melodrama a slick, modernized revamp, pushing the tone and energy even higher. From our early hands-on, Persona 4 Revival delivers the original with renewed vigor, with more expressive character action and new combat mechanics like the Primetime ability to strategically tear through demons with the squad. Revival is shaping up to not only be a great way for fans to dive back into the world of P4, but also to give newcomers a chance to see why the Atlus RPG is one of the greats.

Remaining Grace presents a very different type of detective story – one that's all about reassessing the bonds left behind in life after your death. From developer Ambedo Studios, this ghost-detective story follows Grace Tao as she seeks to solve the mystery of her own death three years later. After reawakening as a spirit, she'll use her new ghost powers to imprint onto objects and people to see new perspectives, piecing together the delicate timeline surrounding her death. Along the way, Grace will learn how her family and closest friends have tried to move on, bringing her closer than ever to the ones who still remember her.

Ambedo Studios' Remaining Grace was the most emotionally rich and captivating game I played at PAX West 2026, and it really leans into its concept of an emotionally compelling detective story about the bonds and community we build through life. It's such a compelling hook for a narrative adventure game, and I cannot wait to see more of it.

Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World

Much like the Pokémon series, the Dragon Quest series also dives into games that are all about collecting monsters and training them to be the very best. With the latest entry of the Dragon Quest Monsters sub-series, The Withered World blends the monster-collectathon and turn-based party battle gameplay with Dragon Quest's stylized, high-fantasy storytelling that's powered by the art style of legendary artist Akira Toriyama. The Withered World shakes things up by leaning further into the experience of the key protagonists, Bianca and Nera, and how their unique abilities will shape their style as capable monster wranglers.

Along with healing a decaying world and recruiting new monsters, you'll also learn the new synthesis skill to merge many of the familiar Dragon Quest monsters into new creations. Boasting over 500 collectible monsters to train and evolve, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World presents the sub-series' most ambitious turn yet, which totally leans into the wacky and heartwarmingly adventurous side of the Dragon Quest series.

For more on Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World , check back with IGN for our upcoming preview.

Coming from developer Causeway Studios, The Final Cut of Lilith Cunningham is equal parts a spotlight for the enduring full-motion video (FMV) adventure game and a psychological thriller where you'll "re-edit" reality to find the protagonist's missing daughter. Blending live-action video with fully explorable environments that match the darkly-surreal atmosphere of a David Lynch neo-noir film, you'll explore a seemingly abandoned motel with a looming supernatural presence. While piecing together clues and finding a mysterious film reel that lets Lilith re-edit the timeline of reality, she'll use her Alan Wake 2 -style mind powers to bend reality to fit a narrative and uncover the truth behind her daughter's disappearance. Even with its brief teaser of what's to come, The Final Cut of Lilith Cunningham is building an eerie, mesmerizing mystery thriller that delivers on its retro-adventure concept.

The upcoming Castlevania: Belmont's Curse is really going all in on being the sort of revival that the Castlevania series needs – and it's doing that by bringing the series back to its 2D action origins. Developed by Evil Empire, the creative team behind Dead Cells and The Rogue: Prince of Persia , Castlevania: Belmont's Curse is the direct sequel to Dracula's Curse and follows Rose Belmont's adventure through a monster-corrupted Paris. The developers are a fantastic fit for the series' style, and their latest game aims to blend classic Castlevania with the sprawling search-action of the action-RPG era, with hits like Symphony of the Night and Aria of Sorrow . Playing Belmont's Curse hits all the right beats of fast and measured combat and satisfying traversal action that the high points of the series have nailed. It's already shaping up to be a worthy comeback for one of Konami's most celebrated franchises.

The interactive visual novel genre can offer dense, truly imaginative storytelling. The upcoming Rain98 is a new narrative work that has its sights set on telling a story that's all about its two protagonists forming a bond as they resolve to save the future -– all while keeping their apartment clean and working a part-time job. Set in an alternate 1998, you play as a mysterious figure from 2025 transported to the past. Meeting up with the mysterious Reina, you bond over the anxieties of a bleak future for humanity and seek to change it with a mysterious ritual. Rain98 's atmosphere channels the dark tone of classic Shin Megami Tensei, all while leaning into the personal story of two lonely youths worried about the future, and it's a compelling narrative that'll keep you engaged for what's to come.

The Nintendo 64 collectathon-style action platformer and the tense, atmospheric soulslike seem like total opposites. But the upcoming Mouseward from developer Finite Reflection Studios seeks to blend these contrasting genres to build a new type of retro-inspired 3D platformer with a stoic action-RPG twist. In Mouseward , you take on the role of a reawakened royal mouse guard tasked with restoring a corrupted kingdom and slaying dangerous foes lurking within. Injecting that plucky and bouncy sense of action into measured, challenging combat can be a tricky concept, but Mouseward is surprisingly effective at delivering on its rhythmic pace and sense of adventure – all with the style of a classic N64 game that's channeling the tone of Bloodborne . It's a neat concept, and the developers behind Mouseward are proving that this genre mashup can work if it focuses on getting players to explore and uncover the weird dangers tucked away in the world.

Ballgame is one of the strangest, yet delightfully challenging puzzle platformers I've seen in some time. Playing as a sentient golf ball named Dolf that's able to defy gravity and twist about in the air, you're tasked with clearing a variety of stages that are filled with weird hazards and other obstacles – and you'll need to do it with as few hits as possible. Just when you're finding your flow and effortlessly blitzing through stages, Ballgame tosses in some bizarre challenges that open up many deftly designed obstacle courses that'll have you planning your moves to make the best run. It's a deceptively challenging 2D puzzle-platformer, but one that I found so incredibly charming to play.

While you're here, check out these previews of other big upcoming games we've played recently!

Alessandro Fillari is a longtime games media professional. Talk video games with him on BlueSky at @afillari.bsky.social .

articles.title: Gundam: Rogue Orbit is an Action Game for Action Game Sickos and a Gundam Game for Fans New and Old Alike | IGN Preview
articles.summary: Action games –well the great ones, anyway – are defined by three things: speed, precision, and player expression. A good action game might do one really well. The great ones have two of them. The all-timers nail all three. This is a preview, so I’m not ready to call Gundam: Rogue Orbit a great action game. But if what I played at Gamescom is any indication, it might just get there.
articles.body:
Action games –well the great ones, anyway – are defined by three things: speed, precision, and player expression. A good action game might do one really well. The great ones have two of them. The all-timers nail all three. This is a preview, so I’m not ready to call Gundam: Rogue Orbit a great action game. But if what I played at Gamescom is any indication, it might just get there.

My Rogue Orbit demo was pretty simple: I would choose one of three pre-baked Gundam loadouts, and my pilot, RE-X, and his partner-in-crime VII would enter the cockpit. The scene starts with the camera behind RE-X and as he steps into the cockpit, it fuses with her perspective. The distance between the two of you evaporates. Those aren’t RE-X’s hands flexing as he settles into his pilot’s seat. They’re yours. It’s a small thing, but it’s one of the little details that made my time with Rogue Orbit work, and something producer Yuya Tomiyama and director Yoshiyuki Serizawa told me the team they spent a lot of time working on because players had said they wanted to feel that they were actually getting into the Gundam and going into battle.

Once snugly seated in my cockpit, I was off to my first mission. The Apocalypse – a group of scary, alien monsters – had invaded a spaceport, and it was up to me, my Gundam Helix, and my buddy Elaine and her Calice to take them down. After getting shot onto the spaceport by what looks like a giant railgun mounted to our ship (sick), it was time to layeth the smacketh down on some poor Apocalypse fools.

Rogue Orbit is quick; the loadout I selected was equipped with the Assault Sword, a close-ranged weapon with abilities designed to close the distance between you and Apocalypse beasties and dish out the hurt while you do it. Your Gundam is big and bulky, and there’s definite weight to it, but it’s also quicker than fast and you can easily use your boosters to slide around the levels as you cleave through Apocalypse monsters. I’d describe boosting as the kind of movement you’d see in an Armored Core game. You’re still on the ground unless you make an active effort not to be, but you’re cruising.

Clearing out the spaceport was pretty easy between my sword, special abilities, and rifle, and the level was pretty linear, but I didn’t mind. Where things really got interesting was the boss fight against a Giant, a massive member of the Apocalypse who has definitely never skipped his arm, chest and back workouts at the gym, but goes a little lighter on leg day. He was substantially bigger than my Gundam, but that just meant there was more of him to hit. I deployed my Slyphid AP-U – Apocalypse Unit, special weapons designed for fighting the Apocalypse – and watched as half a dozen little drones swarmed him with lasers. Helpful, but they wouldn’t win by themselves. I needed to take it to him, too.

It’s in these big fights that Rogue Orbit feels like it’s going to be at its best. I had to manage my heat, which you build from moving, dodging, attacking, and using abilities and make sure I wasn’t getting walloped. It’s pretty easy to mash in Rogue Orbit if you want to (just like any action game), but it’s not ideal, and you’re actively rewarded for being precise and picking the spots to use your abilities, which not only cost heat, but individual charges that recover gradually over time. I could have spammed the Assault Blade’s charged heavy attacks and abilities, but I would have overheated and wasted all my charges. Playing smart was key.

And I was rewarded for that, too. In addition to a health bar, bosses have a stagger meter that builds separately. When I filled it, the Giant fell to his knees and I got to whale on him. It was a perfect time to pop my abilities, land those heavy attacks, and use an AP Unit Burst, a devastating attack based on the AP Unit you have equipped. In the case of my little drones, they would swarm around the enemy like the biggest, angriest bees you’ve ever seen. Pretty rad.

But my favorite part of the fight was when I lopped the Giant’s arm off. See, you deal specific damage to body parts in Rogue Orbit, even if you can’t lock onto them directly. I didn’t know that at the time, but it turned out well for me because losing his arm also meant losing any attacks associated with it. I hadn’t just accomplished a cool visual feat. I’d functionally changed the fight. Tomiyama and Serizawa told me that was a core part of Rogue Orbit’s design.

“You can plan your strategy and also you can learn about the enemies; the way you want to attack, for example. Some enemies have weaknesses around wings or [arms]. So you can really customize yourself and you can learn about the target and you can plan your attack, as well. As you play, you sort of feel good about certain attacks. ‘I like using this one, I like to attack like this.’ So you start learning about it and you actually master your own skills.” All of that came to a head in the demo’s second part: a fight against the Drake, a massive, dragon-like monster that could fly. This time, I went in with the whip sword, which could change form between a sword and a whip. It was kinda like playing Ivy from Soul Calibur, just as a robot. I adore it. Want to attack from range and look cool as hell doing it? You got it. Take out a whole gang of Apocalypse (Apocali?) at once. Done deal. And it’s a sword for the up-close-and-personal beatdowns? Be still my beating mecha heart. But the cool thing is the whip mode works great up close, too.

Gundam Rogue Orbit Reveal Trailer Summer Game Fest 2026 - Screenshots

That was good, because the Drake was no joke. He could breathe fire, summons these little balls to shoot all kinds of lasers at me, and whack me with his tail. To fight him, I had to meet him in the air, which is where Rogue Orbit’s surprisingly spiffy vertical movement comes into play. You’re not quite as fast or agile in the air as you are on the ground, but I was more than capable of bringing the fight to him.

When I asked about it in our interview (and noted how rare truly 3D movement is in a game like this), Tomiyama and Serizawa said getting it right had been a priority: “That's what we really wanted to work hard on because we have to have the high speed and create movement. That really was a must. But the Gundam is fighting against big enemies. And also we want to create that scale of the Mobile Suits. It's big. So the Mobile Suit has to be [capable] and also the player has to feel good about controlling the Mobile Suit. So that feeling is something that we, again, we have to worry about [realizing] in the game. “This 3D movement was really challenging to actually create, but we really wanted the players to feel good. They want to enjoy controlling the Gundam. And… in order to achieve that, we didn't want to make it complicated because people would give up on it… So in order to get action game functions ultimately, we had great research and it took us a long time to do lots of trials and also we asked the Bandai Namco team all over the world [for their] feedback. We are still making it, but I think we are on the right track in the right direction for that.”

They continued: “The mobile seat is 80 meters high and it's a mobile weapon in itself. So when we create an action game, we don't want this big thing to be slow obviously, but we want the players to feel the weight of it, the weight of the sword, the weight of the actual Mobile Suit. So in order to achieve the balance between the high speed and the mobile seats, again, we really have been working. There is also flexibility. There are functions that you can actually cancel when you're controlling the Mobile Seats. So everything is pretty much a balancing act.”

Based on what I played, I think they’re on the right track. The Drake was much tougher than the Giant, but it also gave me a chance to try out Over-Rise, which temporarily halts Boost Gauge consumption so you can go all out without overheating. It also makes it easier to execute Tactical Moves. Time one right, and you’ll slip out of an attack and right behind the enemy.

All of this feels great, but I also appreciated how much control I had over the fight. Now that I knew I could take out enemy body parts, Monster Hunter-style, I started targeting the Drake’s tail and its wings. Once they were gone, it couldn’t easily take to the air and I didn’t have to worry about its tail if I managed to dodge behind it. I even got to put the other AP-U – a deployable shield that provided cover from the Drake’s scarier attacks – to the test, and it worked wonderfully. I always felt like I had an answer to every issue, and it was a lot of fun figuring out which of my abilities did what, and when to use them.

I finished the Drake off early, so I opted to try it again with the Sword Lance. If the Assault Sword was a close-ranged monster and the Whip Sword emphasized versatility, the Sword Lance was a medium-ranged weapon that emphasized combining heavy attacks with dodge to build charges for a special attack that spawned exploding orbs of energy. I thought it would be right up my alley, but the slower speed and more mid-ranged, defensive style didn’t work for me. I smoked the Drake with the Whip Sword. With the Sword Lance, I had to rely on my healing items. I still got the job done. It was just much harder. But that doesn’t mean that I might not get on with it in the future. According to Tomiyama and Serizawa, I’d be able to customize weapons and the Helix itself to suit my playstyle in the final release.

When I exited the cockpit of the Helix for the last time, I felt good about what Rogue Orbit is shaping up to be, but I also know there’s a lot more to see, and the team is aware they have a lot to live up to. But I think, after speaking to Tomiyama and Serizawa, that’s part of the challenge – and the fun.

“This is [an open] door for new fans worldwide, but I'm aware that there are huge communities of Gundam in America, for example, and they are just so passionate and we haven't talked about it, but this has got all the aspects that make Gundam Gundam,” the producer and director told me. “So hopefully all the die-hard fans will appreciate that.”

Will Borger is an IGN freelancer. You can find him on Bluesky @edgarallanbro.

articles.title: Malibu Sinkhole Threatens to Swallow Hollywood Star Nicolas Cage's House
articles.summary: A massive sinkhole has opened up in the Californian city of Malibu, threatening to swallow up the home of Hollywood star Nicolas Cage.
articles.body:
A large sinkhole has opened up in the Californian city of Malibu, and is threatening to swallow up the home of Hollywood star Nicolas Cage.

The driveway at the front of the property, which reportedly belongs to the National Treasure, Con Air, and Face/Off star, has already fallen below ground. This is due to the approximately 30-by-30-foot sinkhole having emerged after heavy rainfall in the area.

On Monday, the hole had been estimated at around 8ft in size, with residents living nearby telling Los Angeles Magazine that, "at that point, the homeowners were not overly concerned. We thought it could be fixed pretty quickly."

On Tuesday morning, the gap opened up to nearer 30 feet in size, with emergency services being called to the area to attend to a gas leak caused by the event. This widening of the sinkhole is what caused the home’s driveway to collapse, with the building now exposed to further damage.

At least five homes on the street are said to have been deemed unsafe for entry by Malibu City officials, with access limited and the area described as "impassable due to the large portion of the road that has collapsed."

According to the New York Times , Cage bought the property only two years ago for a price of $10.5 million. It stands on stanchions rooted into the oceanbed it mostly hangs over, and it's due to the impact of powerful waves and heavy rain following a hurricane warning that the sinkhole is believed to have started.

Thankfully, no injuries have been reported due to the damage caused.

Nicolas Cage recently insisted that it’s "perfect" that one of his latest projects, Spider-Noir, will only be getting one season's worth of episodes. The Prime Video animated Spider-Verse show was recently canceled by Amazon after viewing figures were shown to have dropped off after an initially strong start.

"For me, one season is perfect, having said what I wanted to say with this dangerous, innovative, pop-art Spider-Man," Cage told Deadline . "Onwards, upwards, inwards." Here's hoping the sinkhole is sorted before anything else heads inwards as well.

Image credits: David Swanson/AFP via Getty Images, Michael Loccisano/Getty Images.

articles.title: Xbox is bringing back startup animations from its console history
articles.summary: Xbox Insiders will also be able to test a new search feature, improved Remote Play quality, and clearer voice chat.
articles.body: Microsoft is starting to test some new Xbox console features with Insiders. Testers will be able to try out custom Xbox boot animations from the past, more personalization options for badges, a new local search feature, improved Remote Play quality, the ability to download while you play on cloud, and clearer voice chat. Xbox testers will be able to pick between the original Xbox One boot screen, the Xbox One X startup animation, the original Xbox Series X / S boot, and the new “we are Xbox” boot animation. Unfortunately you won’t be able to select the original Xbox or Xbox 360 boot animations, it’s only Xbox One onwards. [Image: You will soon be able to customize the Xbox boot animation. [Image: The new local search feature. The new local search feature is designed to find games and achievements in large lists. “Available in My games & apps, official club achievement lists, and profile achievement history, local search works alongside existing filters and sorting options to help players find what they’re looking for faster,” explains the Xbox team. Xbox Remote Play is getting support for up to 1440p resolution and improved bitrates on Xbox Series X / S consoles. If you use Xbox Cloud Gaming, you’ll also be able to allow downloads to continue in the background while you stream games. Downloads will still automatically throttle “as needed,” though. Xbox Series X / S owners will also be able to test Voice Clarity, a feature that “helps reduce everyday background noise.” It sounds a lot like the Voice Clarity feature that’s part of Windows 11, which eliminates echo and other background noise. “Voice Clarity will be enabled by default in party chat and in most games released since 2020,” says the Xbox team.

articles.title: Sunset Overdrive Was the Highlight of the Otherwise-Rough Xbox One Era and Remains Criminally Underrated
articles.summary: There’s no doubt that Insomniac is and should always be proud of Sunset Overdrive. It grinded rails so that Spider-Man could web-swing through Manhattan. Without Sunset, there probably isn’t a Spidey – or at least, Spider-Man wouldn’t have been as incredible right out of the gate as it was. Any of you out there who did play it – sadly, it never got ported to PS4 even after Sony acquired the studio, though it did come to PC in 2018 – are probably nodding your heads in agreement as you read this piece. In my opinion, it is the very best Xbox One exclusive that would’ve stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the very best PlayStation 3, 4, or Xbox 360 exclusives.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

When I started this Xbox retrospective project ahead of the console’s 25th anniversary this November, I knew it’d skew heavily towards original Xbox and Xbox 360 games. And while the Xbox One era wasn’t all bad, it was nonetheless one that a lot of Xbox fans would be happy to fast-forward through. Sure, the platform and messaging woes get most of the blame for Xbox’s first failed console (and before the Xbox faithful come after me, Nintendo’s had one too: anyone remember the Wii U? And heck, Sony had the Vita), but the lack of first-party games – let alone good ones – had as much to do with the Xbox One being a rough generation for Xbox as anything else.

Still, there were diamonds in the rough, and one of them would’ve been a HUGE hit in the Xbox 360 generation, but instead it was released on the wrong console at the wrong time. That game is Sunset Overdrive. On paper/in a vacuum, it should’ve been a huge blockbuster hit. Insomniac Games, not yet owned by PlayStation but long an exclusive partner of Sony’s and makers of hits like Ratchet & Clank, was signing with Microsoft to do an exclusive open-world game for the new Xbox One console that was coming hot on the heels of the wildly successful and beloved Xbox 360.

Again, we all know what happened in 2013 with the reveal, the disastrous E3, and then the launch, but for its part, Insomniac held up its end of the bargain. When Sunset Overdrive dropped in the Fall of 2014, it was absolutely brilliant – a rare open-world game not made by Rockstar that had style and substance. Its cel-shaded art style was a perfect fit for the dystopian, punk vibe (with a healthy dash of comedy mixed in!) that Sunset Overdrive brought to the table.

IGN absolutely loved it , and I advocated strongly for it internally in our Game of the Year discussions (speaking personally, nothing against Dragon Age Inquisition but I’m still salty that it beat out Sunset). But as I mentioned, its timing really couldn’t have been any worse. I’m still convinced that if it had either been released on the Xbox 360 (ignoring the technical impossibility of that) or in an alternate universe it had been a Sony-published game on the PS4, it would’ve been a massive, beloved hit. But those are the breaks sometimes. Obviously, very little of Sunset Overdrive’s fate was in Insomniac’s direct control beyond the crucial part, which was of course making an amazing game (but you can read about how it became an Xbox One exclusive if you like).

It was the rare open-world game where every quest felt fun in its own unique way. Navigating around the world via the grind rails took a good 10-15 minutes to adjust to in the very beginning, but once you got in sync with it, you’d zoom around the world, having an awesome time while doing so. It will forever haunt me that we never got a sequel; now-retired Insomniac founder Ted Price told me at the time that the studio wanted to make a sequel . Even more interestingly, he also told me that it was originally more like Fortnite. Who knows, maybe that decision haunts Insomniac!

But regardless, there’s no doubt that Insomniac is and should always be proud of Sunset Overdrive. It grinded rails so that Spider-Man could web-swing through Manhattan. Without Sunset, there probably isn’t a Spidey – or at least, Spider-Man wouldn’t have been as incredible right out of the gate as it was. Any of you out there who did play it – sadly, it never got ported to PS4 even after Sony acquired the studio , though it did come to PC in 2018 – are probably nodding your heads in agreement as you read this piece. In my opinion, it is the very best Xbox One exclusive that would’ve stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the very best PlayStation 3, 4, or Xbox 360 exclusives.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Hear Me Out: A $1,000 Robot Vacuum Might Actually Be Worth the Investment
articles.summary: After owning one for over three years now, I can honestly say I'd do it again.
articles.body:
Robot vacuums have come a long way since the first models entered the market years ago. A lot of people tried using one before, didn't appreciate the limitations, and swore off robot vacuums entirely. Today's robot vacuum, however, is an entirely different breed. The highest end models are exceptional cleaning aides and are worth a new look.

You can always buy a cheap robot vac, but I wouldn't recommend it in the end. Cheaper options don't last as long and don't offer as much value as newer models, so you may be disappointed in the long run. If you don't want to pay a lot of a robot vacuum, that's understandable. I am just of the opinion that getting a budget robot vacuum won't satisfy your everyday needs. If, however, you're willing to invest in some frankly cutting edge tech, then you have a good chance of finding a vacuum that fits your lifestyle. You don't have to buy the most expensive or highest end models, but when it comes to robot vacuums, you do get what you pay for. And cue the new ECOVACS DEEBOT X12S OMNICYCLONE .

Save $300 Off the ECOVACS DEEBOT X12S OMNICYCLONE

ECOVACS DEEBOT X12S OMNICYCLONE Robot Vacuum & Mop

The DEEBOT X12S OMNICYCLONE was unveiled during IFA 2026 . It's ECOVAC's most powerful vacuum to date and also the first to be SGS-certified (more on that below). It retails for $1,299.99, but Amazon currently has it on sale for $999.99 with free shipping after a $300 off instant discount. That doesn't make the X12S inexpensive, but it's laundry list of advanced features, top-notch performance, and automated functionality help justify the price tag.

The X12S is both a vacuum and a mop, and it excels at both. But let's start with the vacuum. It boasts 27,000Pa of suction, equivalent to about 53 air watts of cleaning power similar to a standard hand vac. The Zero Tangle 4.0 roller brush with stiff bristles pushes down into carpet pile instead of sitting on top, allowing the vacuum to more easily penetrate past the carpet fibers to the debris that's hidden below. The X12S is SGS certified to remove an average of 97.44% of dust, mites, dander, and allergens from carpet, something that can't be said for most robot vacs out there, regardless of price.

Moving on to the mop side, the X12S utilizes its patented OZMO Roller 3.0 system, which comprises of a single microfiber brush that spins vigorously at speeds up to 220RPM to scrub off stubborn grime. Thirty two micro-nozzles continually spray clean water across the roller to keep it moist. The dirty water is scraped up and then suctioned into a separate holding tank for disposable once the X12S returns to the dock.

The X12S features a unique dock as well. Whereas most other self-emptying docks I've seen empties the dust bin into a disposable vacuum bag that you have to change (pretty often), the X12S dock sucks the dirt into a canister that can be emptied out in a garbage can. That's right, you can take vacuum bags out of your budget. The roller is washed with hot water and then dried with 145°F heated air. The dirty water gets collected in one bin and a second bin refills the robot with clean water. The docking station can also dispense cleaning solution, self-clean, and self-dry to reduce routine upkeep.

The X12S navigates your floors and avoids obstacles all while mapping your entire layout using a combination of LIDAR and RGBD cameras. The TruePass adaptive 4-wheel-drive climbing system can also navigate over floor transitions as high as 1.6". ECOVACS has a mobile app that unlocks all of the smart features on the Deebot X12S, including scheduling, maintenance, updates, and manual controls. You can set up no-go zones or have the X12S run during the times and days that you're not home, and more. The app will alert you when service is required, whether it be simple maintenance or parts replacement. All parts that are intended to be serviced y can be purchased from Amazon.

I paid $1,100 for a robot vacuum back in 2023. I had tried quite a few cheaper robots from many brands before then and I had come away disappointed every single time. The one I finally ended up being happy with happened to be the most expensive. I had buyer's remorse for the first month or so, until I realized just how dirty my floors were and how quickly they got dirty again. Three years later, I feel like it was well worth the money spent. My robot vacuum is still running strong and I hope it will last a few more years. The technology recently has evolved greatly and I wouldn't hesistate buying another premium robot vacuum once I need to. If that time is near, the X12S would be one of the top contenders on my list.

articles.title: The New SteelSeries Aeon Pro Wireless Gaming Controller With Infinite Battery Life Is Now Available
articles.summary: Quite possibly the best wireless PC and Xbox gaming controller ever.
articles.body:
SteelSeries just announced its new Aeon Pro wireless gaming controller for PC and Xbox and it's already available to purchase at the Steelseries online store for $259.99. At that price, we'd be asking a lot from our controller: top-tier build quality and a plethora of features, maybe even some unique to this controller. Fortunately, the Aeon Pro delivers.

Now Available: SteelSeries Aeon Pro Gaming Controller

SteelSeries Aeon Pro Gaming Controller for Xbox, PC

SteelSeries already has a lineup of gaming controllers that includes the Stratus and Nimbus. The Aeon Pro, however, is the company's first high-end pro-grade controller. Honestly, it's shaping up to be one of the best PC and Xbox controllers ever. IGN's Bo Moore has already posted his Aeon Pro review-so-far and his initial impressions have been stellar.

Amongst the bevy of features packed in the Aeon Pro, one stands out in particular, and that's the infinite battery system. This is essentially a hot-swappable battery system much like what you'll find in the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro and Omni headsets, which I consider to be one of the best gaming headets on the market for this reason. The Aeon Pro basically includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your controller and the other to remain charged and ready to go in the docking station that doubles as a charger. You get wireless freedom with zero downtime .

The Aeon Pro's other standout feature is its patented QuickSwitch system. You can switch between Xbox, PC, or mobile instantly and seamlessly, with no re-pairing or re-plugging required. How does that even work? It's pretty simple, actually. In addition to being a charger for your batteries, the docking station is also a hub of sorts. You plug your Xbox and PC via USB Type-C ports on the rear, and the controller then connects wirelessly to the dock. For mobile, the connection is made via Bluetooth. Again, I've seen this technology before in the Arctis Nova Pro Omni headset, and SteelSeries carried this feature over to the Aeon Pro. That's a big brain move.

Hall effect and micro-switches throughout

My favorite gaming controllers in the past have two features they all have in common: Hall Effect joysticks and mechanical switches for nearly all of its buttons (including the d-pad). The Aeon Pro does not disappoint. Both joysticks use Hall Effect magnetic sensors. These are superior to traditional potentiometer-based analog sensors. In addition to being more precise and more sensitive, they have no moving parts that can wear out and are thus naturally resistant to stick drift.

16 total buttons all customizable through the OLED display or GG app

The Aeon Pro has a d-pad and twelve programmable buttons, all of which use satisfyingly clicky mechanical switches. These include: four XYAB buttons, four trigger buttons, and four rear paddle switches. Two of the trigger buttons also feature adjustable travel length; with a flick of a switch you can choose either full travel or a hair trigger. The buttons can all be customized using the OLED display on the controller or via the Steelseries GG app.

Are you a sucker for interchangeable thumbsticks? The Aeon Pro has got that too. Included in the package are four different styles of modular thumbsticks that you can swap out: convex, concave, standard length, and long. They simply snap onto either joystick position and are a nice touch that you'll only find in premium controllers.

It's not cheap, but few great things are.

I've seen and tested so many tournament controllers, but none with all the technology that's packed into the Aeon Pro. Yes it's expensive, but if you're a heavy gamer that uses a controller for hundreds of hours, then this is so worth it.

articles.title: Callina Liang's Stunt Double in the Street Fighter Movie Had to Wear Butt Pads to Match Chun-Li's Physique
articles.summary: Callina Liang’s stunt double in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie had to wear butt pads in order to realistically match Chun-Li’s muscular physique.
articles.body:
Callina Liang’s stunt double in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie had to wear butt pads in order to realistically match Chun-Li’s muscular physique.

Director Kitao Sakurai revealed this humorous anecdote during a Q&A session at a media event ahead of the movie’s official release. The topic was the intense training Liang underwent to achieve Chun-Li’s iconic thunder thighs, which grew her legs by 6.5 centimeters.

In fact, Liang’s silhouette had gotten so muscular that her stunt double couldn’t convincingly pull off her physique for action sequences — so she had to wear butt pads to make her glutes match the results of Chun-Li’s rigorous squat routine.

“I knew it was serious when we were filming a scene kind of later in the movie, and I saw Callina’s stunt double, and I was like, ‘What are you wearing?’ And there were like these butt pads that she had to wear just to match Callina’s physique,” Sakurai said.

Noah Centineo, who plays Ken Masters, chimed in: “Yeah, and then we had to wear them out of solidarity, too.”

Whatever it takes to become Chun-Li. 🫡 #StreetFighterMovie pic.twitter.com/NKDopb5iqT — Street Fighter Movie (@Street_Fighter) September 8, 2026

Whatever it takes to become Chun-Li. 🫡 #StreetFighterMovie pic.twitter.com/NKDopb5iqT

Liang has been open about the work it took to bring Chun-Li to life, saying she took on a grueling martial arts routine and even ate a dozen eggs every single day to gain enough muscle mass.

"Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu). I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each,” she said in an August interview with Empire Magazine.

That’s not all; Liang also says she downloaded every version of Street Fighter available on her PlayStation 5 and recorded Chun-Li’s moves on her phone to get a better feel for how the First Lady of Fighting Games moves in battle.

Street Fighter releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. For more on the movie, you can check out our in-depth interview with David Dastmalchian , who plays the movie’s iconic villain, M. Bison, where he told us all about how he went on a deep dive into cult leaders throughout history to bring the psycho-powered dictator to life.

The cover art is an Al Williams piece from Star Wars: The Early Adventures.

This book was just released back at the end of July, so this is the first substantial discount the collection has received since then.

Star Wars Legends: The Newspaper Strips Omnibus

These comics were first published starting in 1994 with Star Wars: The Early Adventures, and issues #1-9 are available here, continuing the story from Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope that introduced the world to the iconic galaxy in 1977. You'll also get Star Wars: Han Solo at Stars' End (1997) #1-3, Classic Star Wars (1990) #1-20, Star Wars: A New Hope (1994) #1-2, Star Wars: The Vandelheim Mission (1995) #1, and the classic Star Wars newspaper clips The Constancia Affair, The Kashyyyk Depths, and Planet of Kadril.

This tome of a time capsule is larger than your average comics omnibus, so be sure to make plenty of space on your shelf to display the vibrant spine in all its glory.

There has been a lot of Star Wars content since the original films were released, but not everything is considered canon these days. Ever since Disney took over the rights to Star Wars back in 2012, pretty much everything that came before has been turned into Star Wars Legends. These "Legends" now exist outside of canon and take place in a universe where the sequel trilogy never actually happened. So these comic strips, alongside some of the best Star Wars Legends books , are no longer officially part of Star Wars lore.

articles.title: Attack on Titan is Coming to 4DX Theaters, But There's a Catch
articles.summary: Attack on Titan is coming to theaters this fall, bringing the beginning of Hajime Isayama’s groundbreaking story and its harrowing end to 4DX and ScreenX cinemas in Japan.
articles.body:
Attack on Titan is coming to theaters this fall, bringing the beginning of Hajime Isayama’s groundbreaking story and its harrowing end to 4DX and ScreenX cinemas in Japan.

September 9 has been officially recognized as Attack on Titan Day in Japan, and to celebrate, two movies compiling the first half of the iconic anime’s first season and its finale are coming to theaters. The catch is that these showings are only in Japan, and they aren’t your run-of-the-mill movie theaters; Attack on Titan Part 1: Guren no Yumiya is heading to cinemas for ScreenX, 4DX, and Ultra 4DX screenings.

If you’re familiar with 4DX, you’ll know that this is kind of wild. If you aren't, it’s a unique type of screening that takes place in theaters with special features like chairs that rumble, gusts of wind, water splashes, and other effects that make the viewing experience so immersive it’s like being on a theme park ride. (You’ve probably seen those viral videos from 4DX screenings of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey — they’re an intense thrill ride, and one that AoT fans won’t want to miss.)

Prepare to rappel off towers and roofs with the Scouting Legion’s 3D Maneuver Gear, flee from oncoming titans, and dodge flying debris — not to mention braving the steam that pours off of the Colossal Titan when it kicks through the walls of Shiganshina.

These screenings are listed for October 23, 2026, but don’t worry if you can’t make it to Japan in time to catch the show; Attack on Titan: The Last Attack, a film compilation of the series’ epic finale, is also coming to ScreenX cinemas in 2027, though no specific date has yet been listed.

ScreenX is different from 4DX in that it shows films on three panoramic screens, making it feel like viewers are totally surrounded by the action. We can only imagine how intense this type of screening will be for Eren’s terrifying final transformation and the all-consuming chaos of the Rumbling.

This is one of several fun activities planned for Attack on Titan fans. Taking inspiration from the Nine Titans, Kodansha is also organizing 99 special events, including making the first 99 chapters of the manga free on its Magapoke app for 99 hours ending on September 13.

Kodansha has even made an official YouTube channel specifically for Attack on Titan, which will host “exclusive content for fans worldwide, including limited-time anime streaming and special videos you won't find anywhere else.” Currently, it’s streaming episodes from Season 1 every Wednesday, though these are only available to viewers within Japan.

There’s a lot to look forward to in the coming weeks if you’re an Attack on Titan fan. This is the latest big news to come from the franchise after Eren’s English voice actor, Bryce Papenbrook, said he was so dedicated to convincingly selling one of the show’s most iconic moments that he literally unhinged his jaw to portray his character’s emotional pain.

In related news, Attack on Titan 3 was shown off at Summer Game Fest this year and is set for release this December. Like the games before it, players will be able to make their own character and experience the events of the Rumbling firsthand in this video game adaptation of the critically-acclaimed anime series.

articles.title: Ace Combat 8 Dev Says Tasha Was the Game's 'Most Expensive' Character to Design
articles.summary: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve Brand Director Kazutoki Kono says developers spent so long working on Tasha that she ended up being the “most expensive character” in the entire game.
articles.body:
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve brand director Kazutoki Kono joked that developers spent so long working on Tasha that she ended up being the “most expensive character” in the entire game.

Kono visited China for the first time to answer questions in a group interview with the media following a hands-on demo for the game, where he opened up about how popular Tasha has become over the last few months.

The pink-haired pilot is a fan favorite, and the game hasn’t even come out yet; set to release on October 2, oodles of future players are already obsessed with Tasha Severskaya , a former “star pilot in Yuktobania's acrobatic team, Zvezda.” Tasha hopped aboard the Endurance to capture publicity footage, but the ensuing war kept her on the vessel, and now she’s part of the Joker Flight squad.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve - June 2026 Screenshots

Speaking with the media, Kono admitted that he was surprised by how popular Tasha had become on social media, revealing that he’s personally on “Team Kate Evans ,” the Lieutenant Commander and leader of Queen Flight. He also revealed that Tasha took the longest to develop out of any other character in the game, since the team kept tweaking different aspects of her design to make sure they got her just right.

“Work on Tasha started relatively early, and she was originally designed by a different artist. She is also the character that took the longest to finalize. Her story and direction were already set, but we kept modifying various aspects afterward, making her the character we refined the longest during development. That's why inside the development team, we jokingly call her 'the most expensive character,'” he said, per Invenglobal .

As for why she’s so popular, Kono thinks it has to do with her fashion sense, saying her pink hair and outfits reflect trends that are currently popular among fans.

“I think elements like her personality, outfit, and especially her sense of fashion in wearing military attire so uniquely happened to fit current trends well, which contributed to all the attention she received,” he explained.

We got the chance to preview Ace Combat 8 this summer, with IGN’s Will Borger saying it was a "very grounded game" that left him “satisfied, but knowing [he] still had so much more to do.” He also got to speak with the devs about their ambitious plans for the game’s multiplayer , which will include 100-player lobbies, several different mission types, and a co-op warfare mode.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve releases on October 2, 2026 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam.
